V18 min · reading

The story

Read one part at a time, aloud. Words with a dotted line have a translation — put your mouse on them. After each part, answer: What is different now?

Part one · The house of ash

Once upon a time, there was a young woman called Cinderella. She lived in a large house with her stepmother and two stepsisters.

When Cinderella was a child, her life was happy. Her father loved her very much. But after he died, everything changed. Her stepmother was cold and unkind. Her stepsisters were lazy and proud. They wore beautiful dresses, went to parties, and spent money on pretty things. Cinderella did all the work in the house.

Every morning, she got up early. She cleaned the rooms, washed the clothes, cooked the food, and made the fires. In the evening, she often sat near the kitchen fire because she was tired and cold. Her clothes were old, and her hands were never clean for long.

But Cinderella did not become cruel. She was quiet, patient, and kind. She often felt lonely, but she did not lose hope.

Part two · The letter and the fire

One day, a letter arrived at the house. It was from the palace.

“The prince is having a ball,” said one stepsister. “All the young women in the kingdom are invited!”

The sisters were very excited. For many days, they talked only about dresses, shoes, and hair. Cinderella helped them prepare. She brushed their hair, cleaned their shoes, and changed their dresses again and again.

“Can I go to the ball too?” Cinderella asked softly.

Her stepmother looked at her old dress and laughed.

“You? To the palace? Don’t be silly. You have work to do.”

On the night of the ball, the sisters left in a carriage. Cinderella stood by the window and watched them go. The house became quiet. She went into the kitchen and sat down near the fire.

For the first time that day, she cried.

Part three · Moonlight

Suddenly, she heard a gentle voice. “Why are you crying, my dear?”

Cinderella looked up and saw an old woman standing near the door. Her eyes were kind, and there was a warm light around her.

“I wanted to go to the ball. But I have no dress, no carriage, and no one to help me.”

The old woman smiled. “I can help you.” She touched Cinderella’s old dress with a small wand. In a moment, the dress became a beautiful gown, soft and bright. Then the woman gave Cinderella a pair of glass slippers. They were strange, delicate, and perfect.

Outside the house, a pumpkin became a carriage, and some small animals became horses and servants.

“You may go to the ball. But remember: you must leave before midnight. At midnight, everything will change back.”

Part four · The dance

When she arrived, everyone turned to look at her. No one knew who she was. Even her stepsisters did not recognise her. They only saw a beautiful young woman in a wonderful dress.

The prince saw her too. He came to her and bowed. “Would you like to dance?”

They danced together for a long time. The music was beautiful, and the palace lights shone like stars. For the first time in many years, Cinderella forgot her sadness. She felt free.

The prince did not leave her side. He liked her because she was not proud. She listened when he spoke, and she laughed in a quiet, honest way.

Part five · Twelve

But then Cinderella heard the clock. One. Two. Three. She stopped.

“What is wrong?” asked the prince. “I must go,” Cinderella said.

She ran from the ballroom. The prince followed her, but she was too fast. On the palace steps, one of her glass slippers fell from her foot. She did not have time to take it. She ran to the carriage and left.

At midnight, everything changed back. The carriage became a pumpkin again. The horses became small animals. Cinderella’s beautiful dress became old and grey. But one thing did not change: the other glass slipper was still on her foot.

Part six · The shoe that fits

The next morning, everyone in the kingdom talked about the mysterious young woman at the ball. The prince wanted to find her. He sent his servants to every house with the glass slipper.

“The woman who can wear this slipper will marry the prince,” they said.

When the servants came to Cinderella’s house, the stepsisters were very excited. One tried to put on the slipper, but her foot was too big. The other tried too, but the slipper did not fit.

Then Cinderella came into the room. “May I try?” she asked. Her stepsisters laughed. “You? Don’t be ridiculous.” But the servant looked at Cinderella and said, “Every young woman in the kingdom may try.”

Cinderella sat down. She put her foot into the slipper. It fit perfectly. The room became silent. Then Cinderella took the other glass slipper from her pocket and put it on her other foot. At that moment, her old clothes changed again into the beautiful gown from the ball. Her stepsisters stared at her. Her stepmother said nothing.

Part seven · After

Cinderella went to the palace. When the prince saw her, he knew her at once. “You came back,” he said. Cinderella smiled. “Yes. This time, I did not run away.”

Soon after that, Cinderella and the prince were married. She left the cold house behind, but she did not become proud or cruel. She remembered what it was like to be lonely and badly treated.

So when she became princess, she was kind to the people around her. She listened to them. She helped them when she could.

And Cinderella finally had a life where kindness was not weakness, and hope was not a foolish dream.

VII4 min · key sentences

Six key sentences

Turn the cards and read them aloud. Then close them and tell the story again with only these six sentences.

VIII10 min · speaking

Let’s talk

Answer like this: your opinion → the reason → an example. Try to use the new words.

Character

Cinderella is kind, but her life is very hard. Is she strong or weak? What do you think?

I think she is… because…

Choice

Cinderella never leaves the house. She waits and hopes. Why does she stay? What can she do?

She stays because… She can…

Family

At the end, Cinderella is not angry with her stepmother. Is this good or bad? What do you say to the stepmother?

I would say…

Love

The prince loves Cinderella after only one evening. Is one evening enough? Why / why not?

In my opinion, one evening is…

Today

Cinderella lives in your city now. Where does she work? Who helps her? She has no wand — what does she have?

Today she works in… Her friend helps her…

You

Did somebody help you at the right moment, like the old woman helps Cinderella? Tell the story.

One day, when I… He / she…

IX2 min · homework

Homework

  • Write 80–100 words. Cinderella writes in her diary the day after the ball. What does she do? How does she feel? Use six new words.
  • Speak (send me a voice message, 1–2 minutes). Tell the story again. Use the six key sentences as your plan.
  • Find and write. Find five irregular past simple verbs in the story (for example: went). Write the infinitive too: go → went.
